kaigo-hygiene-01-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Ask about preferences and assistance needed so the person can choose clothing suited to the activity.
Distinguish permission to take clothing out, what the person plans to do and what has already been done.

kaigo-hygiene-01-knowledge-0.heading: Clothing functions and personal choice
paragraphs: Clothing protects skin and supports daily life suited to seasons and activities. Grooming also relates to daily rhythms, relationships and personal expression. Do not decide by staff preference. Together, check what matters to the person, the season, activity, physical condition and comfort.
For someone with reduced vision, offer verbal descriptions of shape or opportunities to feel fabric according to their wishes. A worker liking a color does not establish the person’s consent.

kaigo-hygiene-01-knowledge-1.heading: Reduce strain on the side that is harder to move
paragraphs: In a hemiplegia example where this method is appropriate, remove clothing from the unaffected side first and put it on the affected side first. The unaffected side moves more easily; the affected side is harder to move because of paralysis or another difficulty. Creating room in the clothing reduces the amount the affected side must move.

Upper garments and pants involve different actions. In sitting, check posture and foot support; in lying, combine agreed position changes. Memorizing the order does not make one method appropriate for everyone.

kaigo-hygiene-01-knowledge-2.heading: Checks after dressing are part of changing
paragraphs: Do not pull limbs forcefully or force painful joints to move. Smooth wrinkles and displacement in clothing and underwear and ask about comfort, pain and changes in condition. Preparing clothes differs from completing a change.
Support locations, applied force and posture changes require individual assessment and training. Learned principles do not replace checking the person’s condition.

kaigo-hygiene-01-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] In their room before a reading event, Morikawa-san is sitting stably and wants an upper garment whose sleeves will not interfere with holding a book. They plan to fasten the buttons themselves. Practice only preparing authorized clothing; do not practice dressing techniques.

kaigo-depth-24.heading: Upper garments in sitting: order and affected-side protection
paragraphs: In a suitable hemiplegia example, put the affected arm through the sleeve first and remove the unaffected side first when undressing. Clothing slack reduces affected-side movement. The correct order does not authorize pulling the shoulder or wrist.

Check condition and consent, then prepare room temperature, privacy and the clothing the person chooses. Check sitting stability; in the example, the worker supports the affected side. Let the person do actions they can, such as unfastening buttons, and help with areas they cannot reach.

When dressing, protect the affected arm while guiding it through the sleeve, then arrange the unaffected side. When undressing, remove the unaffected side first to create room. Finish by adjusting underwear and seams and checking comfort, pain and condition. If a sleeve is tight, consult about clothing or method rather than using more force.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-depth-25.heading: Pants in sitting: separate foot placement from standing
paragraphs: Putting feet through pants and pulling pants up to the waist require different support and balance. In the hemiplegia example, dress the affected side first and undress the unaffected side first. Lifting a foot can disrupt balance, so choose a method matching physical ability.

Establish stable sitting, guide one foot through at a time and let the person pull up as far as possible. Finish in standing only when stable support and necessary help are available. If standing is unstable, use an individually trained method, such as completing what is possible seated or working in lying.

Do not ask someone who stands by holding on with both hands to release support and pull up clothing alone. Avoid having both feet lifted together. Check rolled hems, wrinkles at the crotch and buttocks, fastenings and comfort. Dressing the upper body independently does not establish independent standing.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-hygiene-01-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] In their room before a reading event, Morikawa-san is sitting stably and wants an upper garment whose sleeves will not interfere with holding a book. They plan to fasten the buttons themselves. Practice only preparing authorized clothing; do not practice dressing techniques.
Haruko Morikawa: I’ll be holding a book at the reading event, so I’d like something whose sleeves won’t get in the way.
Care worker: You want something that makes holding a book easy. Are there any clothes you usually wear that you’d like to consider?

Haruko Morikawa: That’s right. If I have trouble, I’ll tell you which part I’d like help with.

kaigo-hygiene-01-transfer-legacy.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Consider another situation] Before listening to music, the person says they want to compare two shawls and choose.

Ask what matters in their choice, obtain permission to take out the two shawls and prepare them. Do not make the final choice for them or treat preparation as completed wearing. Preserve their choice and what they can do independently.

kaigo-hygiene-01-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs:
Note before the reading event

kaigo-language-transfer-225.heading: Distinguish the person’s and family’s opinions
paragraphs: [New practice situation] While preparing to go out, the person tells staff, ‘My daughter suggested the red hat, but I’ll choose the white one today.’ The worker repeats the color the person has now chosen and asks what help is needed to prepare.
The family suggestion is red; the person’s choice today is white. Do not replace the person’s choice with the family suggestion.

kaigo-hygiene-02-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Explain oral care’s purpose, posture, denture care and observation points.
Distinguish labeling facts from unconfirmed ownership and check with the responsible person before use.

kaigo-hygiene-02-knowledge-0.heading: Oral cleanliness and health
paragraphs: Oral care cleans teeth, gums and the mouth and helps prevent tooth decay, gum disease and bad breath. It also supports saliva secretion, prevention of dryness, taste and appetite. Reducing oral bacteria relates to preventing aspiration pneumonia, but does not guarantee prevention.
Toothbrushing, rinsing and denture care are different activities. Check what the person can do and what help is needed according to abilities, oral condition and the plan.

kaigo-hygiene-02-knowledge-1.heading: Posture and supplies for oral care
paragraphs: Assist in a stable posture without excessive chin elevation. When facing the person, consider eye level; when assisting from behind, also support the head appropriately. In the hemiplegia example, watch for food remaining on the affected side when observing the mouth.

Check the plan for rinsing and spitting ability, supplies and water handling. Do not ask the person to rinse or give them water to drink while ability is unknown. Follow the assessed method for alternative supplies when a regular toothbrush is difficult to use.

kaigo-hygiene-02-knowledge-2.heading: Confirm personal dentures before handling
paragraphs: Dentures may be full or partial. Confirm the dentures belong to and fit the person, and clean after meals and store appropriately. Remaining teeth and the mouth also need cleaning, not only the dentures.

Follow the material, product instructions and personal plan for cleaning and storage. Do not independently use boiling water or boiling, or assume ownership from a matching case color. Report pain, swollen gums or bleeding to a healthcare professional and do not forcefully continue actions causing pain.

kaigo-hygiene-02-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You report to nurse Fujino at the supply-preparation table. The denture case body bears Hasebe-san’s name, but the differently colored lid beside it has unconfirmed ownership. Hasebe-san is in their room with the responsible staff member. Do not open it, exchange lids, clean or fit dentures.

kaigo-depth-32.heading: Oral care: control force and observe the mouth
paragraphs: Oral care considers cleanliness, prevention of dryness, taste and appetite. It does not promise to prevent every case of aspiration pneumonia. Check rinsing, spitting and swallowing abilities; do not give large amounts of water while ability is unknown.

The textbook describes having the person rinse first if able. However, establish rinsing ability and water handling beforehand. Prepare personal supplies and stable posture and assist without raising the chin. A pencil-like toothbrush grip helps control force. Check outer, inner and chewing surfaces in sequence and gently brush each tooth. In the hemiplegia example, also watch for food remaining on the affected side.

Choose sponge brushes or other aids for difficulty using a toothbrush through an assessed method. Do not assume they replace every toothbrush function. Observe bleeding, swelling, pain, dryness and remaining material and report necessary information. Brushing does not remove the need for observation; do not force the mouth open.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-depth-33.heading: Dentures: confirm ownership and clean the mouth too
paragraphs: Full dentures replace all missing teeth in a jaw; partial dentures replace some. Their retaining structures differ, so there is no single removal and fitting method. Confirm personal ownership and the method checked by dental professionals.

The textbook’s basic approach is to remove dentures after meals and clean them under running water with a suitable brush. After removal, clean remaining teeth and the mouth too. Removing dentures alone does not complete oral care.

Because dryness may cause damage, the textbook describes storage in a personal case using water or denture cleaner. Apply this according to the material, product instructions and dental guidance. Prevent cleaning solution from being mistaken for a drink. Report pain, looseness, cracks or difficulty eating. Do not force dentures in or bend them to repair them independently.

During removal or fitting, do not pull clasps or bite incompletely seated dentures into position. Check the personal method for holding and positioning them to avoid damage from dropping. Follow dental guidance for nighttime removal and storage rather than assuming identical conditions for everyone.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

paragraphs: [New practice situation] During handoff, a worker reports, ‘The person says their tooth has hurt since yesterday evening. We will contact the nurse and check the appointment arrangement with the person responsible next.’

kaigo-hygiene-03-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Relate skin functions to temperature differences, fall prevention and privacy checks.
Report equipment problems and unconfirmed items. Do not start bringing the person there until checks after corrective action are complete.

kaigo-hygiene-03-knowledge-0.heading: Skin structure and functions
paragraphs: Skin protects the body from external stimuli and harmful substances, receives sensations and helps maintain temperature and moisture. Beneath the outer epidermis is the dermis, containing structures such as sebaceous and sweat glands. Fatty tissue lies below the skin.
Skin folds, where sweat and sebum collect easily, are places where dirt and moisture may be missed. Protect the skin by maintaining needed cleanliness and dryness rather than scrubbing hard.

kaigo-hygiene-03-knowledge-1.heading: Temperature differences and fall risks in bathing
paragraphs: Bathing supports cleanliness, refreshment, relaxation and daily rhythms. However, sudden temperature differences between the bedroom, changing room and bathroom, or high bathwater temperatures, burden the body. ‘Heat shock’ associated with rapid temperature changes is not the same term as heat illness caused by heat exposure.

The textbook also discusses effects of warming on circulation, metabolism, muscle and joint movement, appetite and relaxation. Benefits are not guaranteed regardless of individual condition. Do not omit condition checks or adjustments merely because bathing may help.
Check wet floors, level changes and equipment condition too. Considering temperature alone does not complete fall prevention.

kaigo-hygiene-03-knowledge-2.heading: Checks before bathing
paragraphs: Check condition and wishes, explain the purpose and assistance and obtain consent. Prepare room and water temperatures, floors, level changes, equipment, clothing and the necessary assistance method. Undress using a suitable method, such as stable sitting.

Also check toileting wishes, timing relative to meals and fluid intake against the person’s condition and plan. The same-edition Japanese textbook cautions against bathing when hungry or immediately after meals because of effects on digestion and absorption. Check personal adjustments rather than prescribing identical times or amounts for everyone. Balance privacy with necessary supervision.

kaigo-hygiene-03-knowledge-3.heading: Distinguish sweat glands from sebaceous glands
paragraphs: Eccrine sweat glands are widely distributed and help regulate temperature through sweat. Apocrine sweat glands occur in limited areas such as the armpits. Sebaceous glands secrete oils that help maintain skin and hair surfaces.
Do not treat these as identical glands or assume all sebum should be scrubbed away. Carefully check skin folds and do not overlook moisture left after washing.

kaigo-hygiene-03-knowledge-4.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You check bathing facilities with staff member Kishimoto before bathing. No person receiving care is here. Onodera-san is in the activity room with the responsible worker. The changing-room curtain has come off, and water remains at the bathroom entrance. Room temperature, water temperature and the bathtub are unconfirmed. Do not operate equipment or independently change the bathing method.

kaigo-depth-34.heading: Bath entry and exit: check support and condition changes
paragraphs: Entering the bath, sitting in the water and getting out each need different checks. Wet floors are slippery, and the affected side may float more readily in water. Watch for orthostatic hypotension when standing suddenly from the bath.

The worker checks water temperature and asks the person to check too if able. In the textbook’s hemiplegia example, showering moves from the unaffected hand and foot extremities toward the trunk, and bath entry also starts with the unaffected side. Wash gently with lather and check areas prone to dirt. Follow the individual plan for equipment, support and staffing.

Support posture and the affected side in the water, continually observing expression and condition. With fatigue or lightheadedness, prioritize safety over completing the schedule and seek help. Do not pull an arm to bring the person over the bath edge or make them stand suddenly. Check stability after exit and discuss another hygiene method if this method does not suit them.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-hygiene-04-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Check wishes and skin condition for face washing, hair styling, shaving and nail care.

kaigo-hygiene-04-knowledge-0.heading: Connect grooming with the person’s life
paragraphs: Support face washing, hair styling, shaving, nail care and makeup according to personal habits and wishes. Face washing concerns the face, a different scope from a whole-body bed bath. Observe hair, scalp and skin when choosing supplies.
Even with difficulty raising an arm, a person may style their own hair using a comb with a suitable handle or reach. One difficult part does not justify taking over everything.

kaigo-hygiene-04-knowledge-1.heading: Observe nails and surrounding skin
paragraphs: Long nails can collect dirt or injure skin. However, cutting too short or deeply into both sides also requires caution. Check nails and surrounding skin and report abnormalities to a healthcare professional.

The textbook illustration distinguishes an example with a squared nail tip from cutting too short or cutting deeply into the sides. Knowing the shape does not establish safe ability to perform care. Report abnormalities and stay within your trained scope.

Use clean, suitable personal nail clippers or files within training and the plan. Do not independently cut abnormal nails or wait until causing bleeding to report. Nails softening after bathing does not authorize unrestricted treatment of diseased nails.

kaigo-hygiene-04-knowledge-2.heading: Consent to shaving and makeup
paragraphs: Ask whether the person wants shaving or makeup and how they want facial hair arranged. Do not impose staff appearance standards. Check skin and product instructions and preserve what the person can do.
Do not share electric shavers or cosmetics without checking personal use and hygiene management. Makeup also requires removal before bed and skin care. Help with difficult parts with consent.

kaigo-hygiene-04-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] At 10:15 a.m., Hasebe-san says, ‘The nail on my left thumb catches on my sleeve and bothers me.’ They are seated in their room with a colleague. Consent to inspect the nail has not been obtained, and neither nail nor surrounding skin has been observed. No urgency is specified. Do not prolong questioning; promptly report to nurse Fujino through the facility procedure.

kaigo-depth-27.heading: Face washing: gently clean around the eyes
paragraphs: Face washing removes facial dirt and can support waking and refreshment. For someone unable to wash independently, wiping with a suitably warm towel is one method. Use clean supplies and do not scrub the face or around the eyes.

Check usual methods, temperature and sensation. Understand the textbook’s inner-to-outer eye direction and gently wipe with a clean surface. Do not use the soiled surface on the other eye. Do not overlook behind the ears or the neck, and keep water or soap out of the eyes.

Gently remove moisture and use moisturizing products suited to the person and plan. Put supplies within reach for someone able to wipe independently and help only where needed. Report redness, pain, discharge or other concerns to a healthcare professional. Do not assume it is dirt and keep scrubbing or independently use eye drops.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-depth-29.heading: Shaving: methods suited to skin and products
paragraphs: Keeping or shaving facial hair is the person’s choice. Use an electric shaver according to the product. The textbook example applies the blade surface appropriately and smooths skin wrinkles to avoid missed hair, but one angle or force does not apply to all devices.

Check wishes, skin wounds and equipment cleanliness and function. Let the person do what they can and explain and obtain consent before helping with difficult areas. Do not press on painful areas or repeatedly shave over the same wound.

Stop with new pain, abrasions, bleeding or similar changes, report the condition and confirm the response. Do not prioritize removing every remaining hair. Check skin and equipment afterward; moisturizing also follows suitable products and the plan. Consent to shaving does not extend to new cosmetics or another blade.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-hygiene-05-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Explain differences between full bathing, partial bathing and bed baths, and the scope of consent.
Distinguish declining a full bath from wanting face washing, and report fatigue to the person responsible.

kaigo-hygiene-05-knowledge-0.heading: Hygiene methods and consent scope
paragraphs: Full bathing, partial bathing such as hand or foot bathing, and wiping the body in a bed bath differ in areas and methods. Declining one method does not establish refusal of all hygiene care. Ask about wishes and condition and consult against the plan.
Wanting to wash the face is not consent to genital washing or a full-body bed bath. Explain the specific assistance and check consent for each activity.

kaigo-hygiene-05-knowledge-1.heading: Checks before, during and after bathing
paragraphs: Before bathing, check condition, consent, surroundings and preparation. During bathing, observe water temperature, feet, posture and expression to assess strain. Standing suddenly from a bathtub can cause lightheadedness, so assist while checking stability.

After bathing, gently dry moisture and check changing clothes, dryness, skin and the person’s sensations. Fluids and rest follow abilities and the plan; do not independently recommend a common amount. Do not omit supervision or rush the person to finish on schedule.

kaigo-hygiene-05-knowledge-2.heading: Protect warmth, privacy and cleanliness together
paragraphs: During a bed bath, keep unwashed areas covered. Clean one area, wipe off soap completely, dry with a dry towel and cover it again. Do not scrub hard. Separate clean supplies from used ones.

The genital area readily becomes dirty with sweat and waste. Consider embarrassment and avoid spreading contamination. The textbook’s female cleaning example works from the urethral side toward the anus. For male care too, check remaining dirt and skin and follow a trained method with consent and the individual plan. Report pain or abnormalities to a healthcare professional. Follow facility training for individual methods and protective equipment; do not try techniques from this text alone.

kaigo-depth-36.heading: Hand and foot baths: check posture and temperature for partial bathing too
paragraphs: Hand and foot baths clean selected parts. They may soften nails, but do not replace every function of a full bath or authorize cutting abnormal nails. Check the skin involved and stable posture.

Prepare a basin, water and towels according to the plan, considering spills and avoiding obstructing routes. The worker checks water temperature and asks about sensation. Do not rely solely on the account of someone with reduced sensation. Support hands or feet without forcing knees or shoulders to bend to reach the container.

Wash gently, rinse with suitable water, dry and check between digits and skin folds. Put equipment away too. Do not make water hotter or soak longer to soften nails faster. Consult about methods if there is pain, abnormal skin or difficulty maintaining posture.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-depth-38.heading: Bed baths: check cleanliness, dryness and warmth area by area
paragraphs: A bed bath cleans the body with warm water, towels and necessary soap when bathing or showering is difficult, for example. Whole-body and partial bed baths cover different areas. Stay within the person’s consent.

The textbook shows a sequence of face, arms, chest and abdomen, back, legs and genital area. Posture and assistance follow the person’s condition and plan. Handle genital care separately to avoid returning contamination to cleaner areas. For each area, wash, remove soap completely, dry with a dry towel and cover again.

Water cools during care, so its preparation temperature alone does not establish the towel temperature against skin. Check room temperature and at actual contact, keeping other areas covered for warmth. Observe folds and pressure areas. Do not scrub painful areas or thin skin. Record the area actually completed accurately.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

paragraphs: [New practice situation] The person says, ‘Today I’d rather wash just my hands than have my body wiped.’ The worker listens and decides to consult the responsible person about current condition and assistance. No method has been decided yet.
The person wants only hand washing. Condition checks and consultation about the method are still to come, so the activity cannot be recorded as already approved.

kaigo-hygiene-06-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Understand hair washing, drying and styling as separate activities and preserve the parts the person can do.
Distinguish plans, consent, actions and unconfirmed results during handoff.

kaigo-hygiene-06-knowledge-0.heading: Hair washing, drying and styling are separate activities
paragraphs: Washing hair, toweling moisture away, blow-drying and combing are separate activities. A person may need help with only one while doing the others independently. Also ask about the desired hairstyle.

Use suitable posture and supplies for hair washing, with finger pads rather than nails. Use the dryer according to product instructions without concentrating heat in one place. Silence about heat alone does not establish safety.

kaigo-hygiene-06-knowledge-1.heading: Do not turn schedules into completed-care records
paragraphs: A plan for hair washing at 3:00 p.m. today is not proof that it finished. Separately record who did what, when and the response or results checked.

Hair looking dry does not establish completed washing. Picking up a comb does not establish completed combing. Report unknown results as ‘result unconfirmed,’ rather than assuming the activity was not done.

kaigo-hygiene-06-knowledge-2.heading: The person’s own actions and remaining checks
paragraphs: If the person wants to comb their own hair after drying assistance, preserve that part. Distinguish assistance provided, planned actions and results not yet checked.

Summarizing everything as ‘grooming complete’ can hide unchecked tasks. Distinguish the person’s words, directly observed facts and information checked later with responsible staff. Update the record according to confirmed results.

kaigo-hygiene-06-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You speak to staff member Kishimoto at handoff. You directly confirmed Morikawa-san choosing an upper garment and consenting to its removal from storage at 2:20 p.m. Neither taking it out nor changing has been done. Hair washing at 3:00 p.m. is another team’s plan; the result is unconfirmed. Do not report both activities as complete together.

kaigo-depth-28.heading: Hair and scalp: choose reachable tools and avoid scratching
paragraphs: Hairstyle is a personal preference. Someone unable to raise an arm high may still comb independently with a suitable handle length or accessible position. Observe hair and scalp and choose tools matching the body.

Maintain stable posture without pulling hair forcefully or forcing the shoulder upward. The washing example wets hair, lathers suitable shampoo, washes with finger pads and rinses. Nails can injure the scalp, so do not scratch with them.

Check pain and wishes during drying and combing too. Do not change hairstyles for staff convenience. Do not interpret tangles or scalp redness as a reason to wash harder. Report the condition and check the method. Confirm personal supplies and maintain cleanliness after use.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-depth-35.heading: After bathing: gently dry without concentrating heat
paragraphs: Moisture left on skin makes body heat easier to lose. Gently press with a towel to remove moisture rather than rubbing hard. Check dryness without overlooking thin skin or skin folds.

With privacy, also check behind the ears, armpits and groin. Follow suitable products and the plan for moisturizing and arrange the clothing the person chose. The worker also checks dryer heat. Do not keep hot air on one spot; follow device instructions for distance and use.

Even if the person says it is not hot, that alone is insufficient when sensation is reduced. Rest and fluids also follow condition, abilities and the plan. Do not recommend a uniform amount to someone with fluid restrictions. Report fatigue, lightheadedness or skin changes based on actual confirmation.

This is for checking knowledge. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual plan, equipment and product instructions, and facility training. Do not try unfamiliar techniques from this text alone; consult the responsible person about uncertain points or changes.

kaigo-language-transfer-228.heading: Check the worker and outcome for each activity
paragraphs: [New situation created for learning] During event preparation, staff member Kishimoto says at handoff, ‘I blow-dried Morikawa-san’s hair. They want to comb it themselves later while looking in a mirror. Tanaka-san, the person responsible, is checking whether the comb belongs to them.’ Tanaka repeats, ‘Drying was completed by Kishimoto-san; the styling result is still unconfirmed, and supplies are being checked.’

kaigo-hygiene-07-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Review grooming and hygiene through personal choice, supply checks and safety.
Distinguish not finding something from loss, and do not touch clean items with used gloves.

kaigo-hygiene-07-knowledge-0.heading: Review distinct hygiene activities
paragraphs: Changing clothes, oral care, face washing, partial bathing and whole-body bed baths differ in purpose, area, consent, posture and equipment. Understanding the term bed bath differs from being able to apply force or assist posture in practice.
Distinguish learning explanations from gaining practical skills under supervision. Check with the person responsible about methods you have not yet been trained in.

kaigo-hygiene-07-knowledge-1.heading: Check choice, supplies and privacy together
paragraphs: Preserve independent actions, cover necessary areas, confirm personal supplies and separate clean from used items. The aim of cleanliness does not remove the need for choice and consent.
Protecting privacy does not mean removing planned supervision. Listen to wishes and arrange safety and observation conditions together.

kaigo-hygiene-07-knowledge-2.heading: What is known and what remains unchecked
paragraphs: Choose one issue: mixed-up supplies, touching clean items with used gloves, expanding consent or overstating records. Explain the problem. Consider known facts, remaining checks, consultation and prevention specifically.
A good conversation score does not establish practical safety. Separately review posture, equipment and skin-protective actions as skills needing training.

kaigo-hygiene-07-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation

Searching for a tool is not completed styling; do not independently use new products.

kaigo-depth-26.heading: Changing in lying: pass fabric without pulling the body
paragraphs: Changing clothes in lying combines position changes with passing fabric beneath the body. Dressing the affected side first and undressing the unaffected side first also assume suitable joint condition and posture. Do not use clothing to pull the body or leave the affected arm trapped beneath it.

In the textbook’s hemiplegia example, remove the upper garment from the unaffected side, gather the removed fabric inward and place it under the body. Turn to side-lying with the unaffected side down to remove the fabric, then remove the affected sleeve. Dressing proceeds through the affected sleeve, trunk fabric, permitted position change and unaffected sleeve. This posture is not suitable for every pain or injury.

For pants, ask the person to lift their hips if able, without forcing someone who cannot. Use support and position changes suited to the method. Finish by checking back and side seams, wrinkles, affected-side position and comfort. Do not leave gathered fabric under the back.

kaigo-hygiene-07-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Before seeing family, Hasebe-san wants to style their hair with their own comb marked on the handle. Kenichi Hasebe: I want to tidy my hair before seeing my family. I’d like my own comb with a small mark on the handle.
Care worker: You’d like your own marked comb. Could you tell me where you remember putting it?
Kenichi Hasebe: I think I put it in the small box. Please look only inside that box. I don’t want someone else’s comb.
Care worker: May I check only inside that box? I won’t use someone else’s comb or one whose owner is unknown.
Kenichi Hasebe: The box is empty. Now I think I might have put it somewhere else yesterday. Where was it?
Care worker: Not finding it in the box is different from establishing it is lost. Other places haven’t been checked, so I’ll consult the person responsible about how to search.
Kenichi Hasebe: I hope it turns up before my family comes. But please don’t use someone else’s.
Care worker: I’ll consult the person responsible, making clear we’re still searching and your hair has not been styled. If it is found, I’ll ask again what help you need.

kaigo-hygiene-07-transfer-legacy.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Consider another situation] The person wants their own face towel with a border. The authorized basket contains only towels without a border, whose ownership is unconfirmed.

Check desired supplies and assistance scope. Report what was checked within permission and what remains unknown. Do not establish loss merely because the item was not found or use unknown supplies. Do not expand a face-washing request into consent for a whole-body bed bath; consult the responsible person.

kaigo-hygiene-07-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs:
Support status note
Hasebe-san wants to style their hair with their own comb marked on the handle. It was not found in the authorized small box. Other places are unconfirmed. Loss has not been established. Do not use the comb of unknown ownership. Styling support has not started. Consult the responsible person.

kaigo-language-transfer-229.heading: Check the specific area where help is requested
paragraphs: [New practice situation] A person adjusting their upper garment independently tells staff only the cuff button is difficult: ‘I can do the rest, so please help with just this button.’ The worker checks the location and asks whether help only with that part is wanted.
The request concerns the cuff button. Do not treat it as consent to take over changing the entire garment or all grooming.

kaigo-gap-infection-01-intro.heading: Additional situation: do not spread dirt from hands to clean items
paragraphs: [Simulated situation created for learning] In a handoff area, practice decisions after receiving a used cloth with a colleague. No actually contaminated cloth or personal care is involved. You are wearing used gloves but have not touched the shared screen. Kishimoto, whose hands are clean, has agreed to enter the information. Check sequence, contact locations and hand hygiene according to facility procedures.

kaigo-gap-infection-01-knowledge-0.heading: Routes through hands and objects
paragraphs: Pathogens can pass to others through hands and objects. No infection diagnosis does not establish that a used cloth is clean. Standard precautions consider the contact risks of the task, not only diagnosis labels.
This situation checks routes and responses. It is not practice in diagnosing someone as infected or guaranteeing that all risk has disappeared.

kaigo-gap-infection-01-knowledge-1.heading: Hand hygiene is needed after glove removal too
paragraphs: Gloves help protect during contact, but used outer surfaces may be contaminated. Do not then touch clean items or another person receiving care. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene.

After removing gloves according to facility procedures, perform hand hygiene. With visible dirt, wash with liquid soap and running water. Follow facility training for methods, products and time; reading dialogue does not establish practical skill.

kaigo-gap-infection-01-knowledge-2.heading: Accurately report shared-screen contact
paragraphs: Touching a shared screen with used gloves risks spreading contamination through the screen. If you have not touched it, say so and arrange alternatives such as entry by a colleague with clean hands.

If contact already occurred, report the object and location and check the necessary response under facility procedures. Changing gloves alone does not clean the screen. Do not independently mix disinfectant or report unconfirmed processing as complete.

kaigo-gap-infection-01-knowledge-3.heading: Choose protective equipment according to task risks
paragraphs: Protective equipment depends on risks such as contact and splashes. Gloves, masks, aprons or gowns and eye protection may be relevant, but every task does not require the same set.

Check unknown procedures with the person responsible. Correct protective-equipment use does not remove hand-hygiene or supply-handling needs. Report contact facts sufficiently without guessing a disease.

kaigo-gap-infection-01-words.heading: Infection-control terms and communication
paragraphs: 触れる（ふれる） — Touch: come into contact with an object, body or another surface.
清潔保持（せいけつほじ） — Maintaining hygiene: keeping necessary cleanliness through methods suited to the person.
手指衛生（しゅしえいせい） — Hand hygiene: cleaning hands through washing or appropriate hand disinfection.
手袋（てぶくろ） — Gloves: items protecting hands from contact risks. Used outer surfaces are not necessarily clean.
標準予防策（ひょうじゅんよぼうさく） — Standard precautions: basic infection measures based on risks of contact with blood, body fluids and similar materials, not only on diagnosis labels.
感染経路（かんせんけいろ） — Transmission route: the path through which pathogens reach people.
Useful expression: I won’t touch it while still wearing used gloves.
Useful expression: I’ll report exactly where I touched.

kaigo-gap-infection-01-dialogue.heading: Check contact with a colleague
paragraphs: [Simulated situation created for learning] In a handoff area, practice decisions after receiving a used cloth with a colleague. No actually contaminated cloth or personal care is involved. You are wearing used gloves but have not touched the shared screen. Kishimoto, whose hands are clean, has agreed to enter the information. Check sequence, contact locations and hand hygiene according to facility procedures.
Misaki Kishimoto: I’ll enter the record. Have you touched this screen with the used gloves?
Care worker: Not yet. I won’t operate the screen while wearing used gloves.
Misaki Kishimoto: Please tell me verbally what to enter.
Care worker: I received a used cloth at 9:40. I haven’t moved to the next task yet.
Misaki Kishimoto: I’ve entered it. After removing the gloves, also perform hand hygiene according to facility procedures.
Care worker: Yes. I’ll remove the gloves, perform hand hygiene, then touch clean items.
Misaki Kishimoto: If you had touched nearby objects with used gloves, what would you report?
Care worker: I’d report the objects and locations touched and check the response under facility procedures. Changing gloves alone would not make the objects clean.
Misaki Kishimoto: Please keep that distinction clear. Let’s check uncertain procedures with the person responsible.

kaigo-transfer-cloth-scope-08.heading: Check towels and assistance scope
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] This occurs before receiving the cloth. Hasebe-san wants to wipe their hands independently and asks for help only with the face. Wiping has not started. Permission covers only the basket beside the desk. The personal towel with a blue border was not found; borderless towels have unconfirmed ownership. No practical techniques are performed.
Hasebe-san: I’d like to wipe my hands myself, but please help with my face.
Care worker: Help with only your face, then. Which towel would you like to use?
Hasebe-san: My own towel with the blue border.
Care worker: I haven’t found it in the basket you permitted me to check. I don’t know who owns the borderless one. Would you like to wait until your preferred towel is confirmed?
Hasebe-san: I’ll wait. Please don’t use the towel that’s here.

Care worker reporting to the person responsible: Hasebe-san wants help only with their face and wants to wipe their own hands. The blue-bordered towel was not found in the authorized basket; other places are unconfirmed. The borderless towel has unknown ownership, and they want to wait without using it. Wiping has not started.
Person responsible: I understand the wishes and the search scope. I’ll check the towel’s location and ownership. Let’s not assume it is lost or use what is here; we’ll wait.
Care worker: Understood. I’ll tell Hasebe-san what is confirmed and ask again about the towel and face assistance. I won’t treat this as consent to wipe the whole body.

[Review] Confirm only face assistance without taking over the hands the person wants to clean. Distinguish not found, unknown ownership and not yet performed. Do not independently switch supplies or expand to a whole-body bed bath. Explain consultation results, then check again with the person.

kaigo-gap-infection-01-transfer-legacy.heading: Report choice, permission and contact in stages
paragraphs: [Simulated practice: read cards in order] Before cloth handling, Hasebe-san requests hair styling. You have not asked which comb they want or obtained permission to open personal storage. A box is in front of you; other drawers are closed. Read each answer card only after asking its question.
First question examples: Which comb would you like today? / Could you tell me which comb you’d like for styling your hair?
First answer card: I want my own comb with a mark on the handle.
Second question example: May I check inside this box to look for that comb?
Second answer card: Please look only inside that box. Do not open the other drawers.
Result card: It was not found in the authorized box. Other places are unconfirmed. The other comb of unknown ownership is not used, and the hair has not been styled yet.
Next separate task card: While handling a used cloth, you touched the edge of the screen with used gloves. Screen handling has not been carried out, and work with clean items has not started.
